statement.p: Find a function f(x,y,z) whose level surface f=6 is the graph of the function g(x,y)= 6x+4y.

static.solution:
g(x,y)=6x+4y is the set of all points (x,y,z) satisfying z=6x+4y, or 6x+4y - z = 0. This is a level surface, but we want the surface equal to the constant value 6, not 0, so we can add 6 to both sides to get 6x+4y - z + 6 = 6. Thus, f(x,y,z) = 6x+4y-z+6 has level surface f=6 identical to the graph of g(x,y)= 6x+4y.
Of course, we could also say that the graph of g(x,y) is equivalent to z - 6x+4y = 0, so that f = z-6x-4y+6.
